Maya (Support): @here Acme (Alexa) reporting that after the canary rollout of model-v4.0.1, their function calls are returning schema validation errors and a bunch of empty tool args. They see 400s and a couple 5xxs.
Jeff (Eng): Can you paste the failing curl and the response?
Alexa (Customer): Here is a sanitized request we used from prod: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"model-v4.0.1","input":"Summarize the article","functions":[{"name":"summarize","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"length":{"type":"string"}},"required":["length"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"summarize","arguments":{}}}'``` Response: ```HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{ "error": "schema_validation_failed", "detail": "function 'summarize' missing required parameter 'length'" }``` We're sure our client sends args normally; this started after the canary.
Maya (Support): Customer also reported latency spikes around the same time; billing saw retries which doubled their token usage.
Ricardo (SRE): Checking infra; deploy-bot shows model-v4.0.1 rollout to canary at 2026-03-16T22:12:10Z. No obvious infra errors, but saw a spike in request replays around 22:15 UTC.
DeployBot: model-rollout: model-v4.0.1 promoted to canary group 'canary-12' by @sam at 2026-03-16T22:12:10Z.
Sam (Eng-ML): Quick hypothesis: v4.0.1 introduced a new heuristic that suppresses function args when it deems them redundant to save tokens — bad idea for strict schema enforcement. I pushed the variant-level config; maybe the routing selected the compressed-args variant.
Jeff (Eng): Can we reproduce internally against canary? I'll run the exact payload against the canary endpoint and capture inference logs.
Ricardo (SRE): Also seeing increased 502s from the function routing layer at the same window. Stack shows some requests hitting a fallback model that returns a truncated tool call payload (empty args).
Jeff (Eng): Repro steps for the oncall: 1) curl payload above 2) set header X-Model-Routing: canary-12 3) capture response and model logs: /var/log/inference/canary-12/*
Oncall: Running now, sending results — got the 400 with empty args. Captured trace id trace-0a9c.
Sam (Eng-ML): Attaching quick diff of the change that likely caused this: function-arg-compression enabled by default for v4.0.1; if compression triggered it emits {} instead of explicit args. I'll revert the heuristic flag immediately for canary.
Maya (Support): Customer is asking for ETA to fix and whether we can rollback canary. They have an SLA and billing concerns.
Jeff (Eng): Short term: disable the compression flag for canary-12 (should be hotfix and no infra rollout). If that fails, rollback traffic away from model-v4.0.1 canary to model-v3.9.8.
Ricardo (SRE): I'll move canary-12 traffic to fallback pool and scale up v3.9.8 nodes. Executing now.
DeployBot: routing-update: canary-12 traffic shifted to v3.9.8 at 2026-03-16T22:27:40Z by Ricardo.
Alexa (Customer): Thanks — we're seeing immediate improvement, function args restored and no more validation errors. We'll monitor for billing anomalies.
Maya (Support): Customer confirmed. We should still follow up with a postmortem and billing credit review.
Sam (Eng-ML): I'll open a PR to remove the default compression flag and add a regression test: ensure function args are preserved for any declared required parameters.
Jeff (Eng): Logging action items: 1) Sam PR + test, 2) Postmortem doc, 3) Billing review for Acme credits, 4) Add e2e canary checks that hit function-calling paths. Assigning owners in the thread.
Maya (Support): I'll file the support ticket and keep the customer updated. :thumbsup:
Oncall: Marking thread resolved for now; will reopen if customer sees more errors. :eyes:
